takeaway: Hunter's canal (adductor canal) lies in the distal medial thigh: roof sartorius, floor adductor longus and magnus, lateral vastus medialis; vessels exit at the adductor hiatus.

question.text: Which of the following muscles form part of Hunter's canal?

lines.text: Hunter's canal, also called the adductor canal, is a narrow fascial tunnel in the distal medial thigh.
Its roof is the sartorius, the tailor sewing along the top.
The floor is formed by the adductor longus,
The vastus medialis lies along the outer wall.
The femoral vessels travel through, then exit at the adductor hiatus into the popliteal region.
The sartorius and both adductors are part of the canal, so the answer is all of the above.
